finding: A learned local LEFT-window replaces the fixed immediate-preceding-token rule for simple and adjective-intervening noun phrases.
However, when a locally well-formed role-bearing adjunct such as 'dem Mann' co-occurs with the true event recipient 'dem Jungen', every pure local-window attachment hypothesis becomes ambiguous.
Therefore marker-to-mention attachment alone is insufficient. The next layer must learn event/clause-to-mention argument attachment, i.e. distinguish event arguments from adjunct/background mentions.
The original K14 15/15 harness did not include 'at least one attachment hypothesis survives the hard distractor curriculum' as a required check; this corrected audit records that gap explicitly.
implication: Do not report K14 as fully solving mention attachment. Report it as removing fixed immediate adjacency while exposing argument-vs-adjunct attachment as the next bottleneck.
